column1: #   Referenced is a subset of emitted: every MIOS_* a consumer reads is a name
#   the SSOT resolver emits.  The tree still violates that, so the gate RATCHETS
#   rather than blocking: every referenced-but-unemitted name that exists now is
#   recorded below with a sample location, and the count is pinned by the
#   ceiling.  (The count lives in #!ceiling, not in this prose, which went stale
#   EMITTED also covers a name supplied by a tracked .env projection named in
#   [laws.projection_registry].surfaces, because a consumer that sources one
#   gets the var without the resolver cascade.  That makes this gate depend on
#   check_ipa_enroll_projection, which is what proves such a file is a faithful
#   projection of its SSOT table rather than hand-written (T-1054).
#   VIOLATION if a name appears that is not recorded here -- a consumer would
#   VIOLATION if the count differs from the ceiling in either direction;
#   VIOLATION if the ledger, the resolver or python3 is missing or fails.
#   Why this ledger exists at all: until T-1052 the check scanned with an
#   INTERNAL_PATHS list that skipped usr/lib/mios, usr/libexec/mios, tools,
#   automation, config, docs, installation, usr/share/mios and var/lib/mios --
#   between them every tree a consumer lives in.  It reported
#   "emitted=2879 referenced=0 missing=0  PASS" on every run.  There was no
#   input that could make it fail.  Turning the scan on surfaced these at once;
#   pinning them is how the gate goes live without a 425-item rewrite first.
#   Do NOT add a row to silence a new name.  Either emit it from the SSOT
#   The second column is a sample location and is informational -- line numbers
#   move.  The gate compares the NAME set and the count.
#   #!ceiling is the number of names and it is EXACT.  More is a regression.
#   FEWER is also a failure: fixing a name must be paid for by tightening this
#   number in the same commit, which is how a ledger drains instead of settling.
